newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West spot power steady at low fall levels.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West spot power steady at low fall levels.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-West region held steady at what many saw as low fall or shoulder month levels, industry sources said.
"Our loads have started dropping with the mild temperatures but we haven't yet begun our maintenance period," said one Mid-Western electricity seller.
"We've got no weather, no outages and no news," said another Mid-Western power broker.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), on peak electricity for a 16-hour block for delivery Tuesday was said to be holding steady in the $13.50-15.00 range.
However, line-loading out of the MAPP region was restricting movements out of the area and pushing prices even lower, said one trader who reported offering MAPP export power at $12.75 with no takers.
Off peak next day power in the MAPP region was discussed steady in the $8.00-9.00 range, the sources said.

On-peak prices in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) for Tuesday delivery were said to be discussed steady in the $15.00-17.00, although hourly non-firm power was pegged higher in the $19.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, the sources said.
Off peak power in the MAIN region was pegged in the $13.50-15.00 per MWh range, the sources said.
In the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak power prices for Tuesday delivery were quoted steady in the $14.50-16.50 range, the sources said.
ECAR trade was reported to be relatively thin, with few sellers willing to part with power at the low levels.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), on-peak power for Tuesday delivery was assessed in the $17.50-18.00 range, with off peak power assessed at near $14.00, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
